newsitem.title: INDIA: India call ends firm on reduced supply, gilts weak.
newsitem.headline: India call ends firm on reduced supply, gilts weak.

text.p: A squeeze in funds supply kept call money rates firm through Monday at 8.50-9.25 percent while government securities ended down in thin trade, dealers said.
They said call money was mostly traded in a 8.5-9.0 percent band with some opening deals at 9.0-9.25 percent.
Dealers said the reasons for the tightness were not clear.
"The liquidity position is not such that call money should touch 9.0 percent," said a dealer at a private bank.
"Some major lenders are either off the market or lending only in small quantities."
Some dealers said a bond auction for 30 billion rupees last Monday had reduced the availability of funds and pushed up call money rates from a 4.25-5.0 percent band before the auction.
"It is quite clear from the participation at recent repo auctions that there is a squeeze in funds," said a dealer.
The Reserve Bank of India received only one bid for 20 billion rupees at its last repo auction on Thursday against 18 for 63.6 billion a month ago.
Other dealers said foreign currency deposits whch matured for payment last week led banks to convert rupees into dollars, leading to a temporary cash crunch.
Dealers said higher call money rates had weakened sentiment in the government securities market, keeping prices soft and trades on a low key.
"Sentiment is down at the moment," said a foreign bank dealer. "Traders are waiting for call money to ease to around 5.0-6.0 percent before taking positions."
Dealers said the 12.59 percent 2004 bonds ended Monday at 106.95 rupees against its previous close of 107.02.
The 11.19 percent 2005 eased to 100.41 from 100.44 while the 11.83 percent 2003 moved up marginally to 100.66 from 100.64.
